title: Probing poll frauds
primary_topics: The rationale for and limits of the Joint DoJ-Comelec Panel and congressional investigations into alleged massive cheating in the 2004 and 2007 elections
Why the GMA proclamation and PET dismissal of FPJ and Legarda protests do not bar new investigations -- but also do not allow removal of GMA from office
The distinct and limited purposes of the new probes: criminal prosecution, not removal; and legislative reform, not reversal of proclamation
sub_topics: Joint DoJ-Comelec Panel (Justice Secretary de Lima and Comelec Chair Brillantes) investigating alleged massive cheating in 2004 and 2007 elections; Congress also poised to begin its own probe
Critics: repetitive and partisan witch-hunts; charges already laid to rest by congressional proclamation of GMA and De Castro; legitimacy confirmed by PET dismissal of FPJ and Legarda protests

Rationale for congressional canvass: Congress adds up totals on face of certificates of canvass; passes upon authenticity and due execution only; does not examine ballots or supporting documents; very limited time (30 days from election to June 30 term start)
GMA proclaimed in wee hours of June 24, 2004; took oath June 30, 2004; Sen. Pangilinan as presiding officer responded with Noted to Sotto's demand to open ballots -- Sotto christened him Mr. Noted

PET dismissal of FPJ protest: FPJ died Dec. 14, 2004; widow Susan Poe denied substitution -- not a real party in interest; even if GMA cheated, Mrs. Poe could not be proclaimed president since nobody voted for her; PET hinted De Castro or Legarda intervening could have allowed continuation
PET dismissal of Legarda protest: she ran for and won as senator in 2007; abandoned VP claim by assuming Senate office (cannot hold both simultaneously)

Purposes of new probes: (1) Joint Panel -- determine whether electoral crimes committed and by whom (criminal prosecutions); (2) Congress -- craft or amend legislation on canvassing authenticity and due execution; Constitution authorizes Congress to promulgate canvassing rules

GMA within legal rights to keep silent and decline comment on bare allegations -- any statement could be used against her in subsequent legal proceedings; self-serving declarations cannot be used in her favor

stances.claim: The congressional proclamation and PET dismissals do not bar new investigations -- those proceedings did not examine the underlying ballots for fraud; they were constitutionally limited to the authenticity and due execution of the certificates of canvass.

The new investigations have distinct and limited purposes: the Joint Panel can determine whether electoral crimes were committed (criminal prosecution, not removal); Congress can craft or amend legislation governing canvassing -- neither can reverse the proclamation.

GMA is within her legal rights to keep silent and decline comment on bare allegations -- any statement could be used against her in subsequent legal proceedings, while self-serving declarations cannot be used in her favor.
stances.rhetorical_move: right-to-silence advisory for GMA as potential criminal respondent

notable_anecdotes: Sen. Pangilinan's Noted reply to Sotto's demand to open the ballots during the 2004 canvass -- prompting Sotto to christen him Mr. Noted -- the most memorable single exchange in the entire 2004 canvassing saga.
The PET hint that substitution could have been granted had De Castro or Legarda intervened -- a small but consequential historical counterfactual about the FPJ protest's fate.
Legarda's strategic self-disqualification: by winning a Senate seat in 2007, she was deemed to have abandoned her VP claim -- illustrating how pursuit of a lesser office can waive a greater one.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Joint DoJ-Comelec Panel (Justice Secretary de Lima and Comelec Chair Brillantes) and congressional investigations into alleged massive cheating in the 2004 and 2007 elections, responding to critics who say the charges were already laid to rest. The congressional canvass merely passed upon the authenticity and due execution of certificates of canvass -- it could not examine the actual ballots within the constitutionally limited 30-day period, as illustrated by Senate President Pro Tem Pangilinan's famous 'Noted' reply to Sotto's demand to open the ballots (earning Pangilinan the nickname 'Mr. Noted'). The PET dismissed FPJ's protest because his widow Susan Poe was not a real party in interest (nobody voted for her as president) and dismissed Legarda's protest because she abandoned her VP claim by winning a Senate seat in 2007. Neither dismissal resolved the underlying fraud allegations on the merits. The new probes have limited and distinct purposes: the Joint Panel can determine whether electoral crimes were committed and file criminal cases -- not remove GMA (her term expired June 30, 2010); Congress can craft or amend legislation governing the canvassing process. CJ closes: GMA is within her legal rights to keep silent, since any statement could be used against her in subsequent legal proceedings, while self-serving declarations cannot be used in her favor.
